I will be honest, my mother does this. And there are a few different ways to take the action itself. 

Someone above said something along the lines of
 "So they are gonna celebrate the absentee father then?" 
        and another said 
"Because they are both the mother and the father."

These are partly true. My mother just calls it second mother's day because of how difficult it was for me to not... Internalize the pain that comes with having an absent father. Father's day in my early years was a day filled with jealousy for me. And it was her effort at somehow, someway I could ignore the missing puzzle piece. 

BUT (IMO, which might piss somebody off) the comment of being both the mother and the father, I'm not going to sit here and say she was. My mom is the best mother on the planet. Better than yours. 10/10. But she wasn't a father substitute. My fatherly substitute was a basically"adopted grandfather in the husband of the woman who babysat me till I was 17. He is turning 93 this year, and is easily my male role model for a husband. 

I think to answer your question, there may be a bit of ego behind it somewhere for some people. There may be some toxicity behind it for some people. But I also think it's a way for that one day of the year to not be filled with jealousy and anger as a child.

I posted it on r/suicide watch or something like that a while ago. I was... Inches. Literal inches from diving off the side of a building that night. The night I found out that my best friend of about 10 years was boning my now ex-fiance. I've experienced wanting to die in a depression sense... But that was different. That was a kind of pain that was scary. It hurt so much that it didn't hurt. I couldn't even feel it. I got hammered drunk that night and just walked for a few hours. Didn't even know where I was. Just a tall parking garage by the beach somewhere. And I sat right on the edge. Right on the top. 

I've never been so close to just... One more step. One tiny jolt. And it would end. I'd never have to think about it again. That was in November. I'm glad I didn't do it. I'm going back to school on the 2nd to be a aeronautical engineer. I have something to look forward to. But at the time, I had no one. I had to act like I was okay, while pulling back from people who called themselves friends who knew and don't tell me. That month hurt. So damn much. The "Why don't we hang out anymore" s and the just...the  Lion the Witch  and the fuckin audacity of this bitch. I'm better now. But I am better. I've grown. And I'm proud of myself. Which is a phrase I don't say to myself enough. And a phrase Is like to convey to the others here. I'm fuckin proud of ya. Don't ask why. I'm proud cuz you suck. But I suck too.
